NACS Holster Plan

OpenSCAD model of the wall holder for the Tesla Gen 3 Wall Connector handle: a drum on a square plate, the wand out of the drum's right side at 45° down, hanging on a fixed cleat in the connector's own lock notch. Rendered from holder.scad; the nose profile is Tesla's, from their NACS STEP file.

The full part: ready to print

The v7 fit coupon printed and the wand docks and holds on it (Brian, 2026-09-18: "the last coupon printed great. This is the one."). The full holder is the same cavity and cleat in the whole drum, exported and sliced: holder.stl and holder-print.3mf.

  • Print: 6 h 07 min, 275 g (265 g PETG, 10 g support interface), 267 layers, from a real slice. Same recipe as the coupon (X2D 0.6 nozzle, 0.30 mm, Bambu PETG Basic, textured PEI, tree supports with Support For PLA/PETG on the second nozzle), plus 3 walls and 20% gyroid because it hangs a wand and an 18 ft cable off the wall.
  • Orientation: plate down on the bed, flange and Tesla T up, as the coupon printed. Supports go in the cavity and under the flange ring; the T is a recess in the top face and needs none.
  • Size on the bed: 108 × 108 × 80 mm (the flange and its point reach a little past the base); the part sits left of centre and the prime tower to its right, 22 mm from it (Studio warned that the tower was too close on the 150 mm file, where the gap was 9 mm; the build now checks it). The two nozzles only share the bed from x = 20 mm, so the part is placed clear of that.
  • Base: 4 in square (101.6 mm), down from 150 (Brian, 2026-09-18: "reduce the size so the base is 4 x 4 but make sure to preserve the wand holder size, as this is perfect"). The body shrank round the wand's cavity: drum Ø100 to Ø80, flange Ø124 to Ø104, Tesla T 70 to 59 mm. The cavity, the cleat, the 1.25 in cleat depth and both wand angles are untouched, and the docking and hold check gives the same numbers as the printed coupon's cavity. The depth stays 80 mm: the cavity alone is 65 mm tall measured out from the wall. Ø80 is about as small as the drum goes; at Ø72 the cavity's far corner is 3 mm from the drum's surface.
  • Solid around every screw hole: a Ø25 region through the plate at each hole prints at 100% infill. Measured in the sliced G-code between the plate's skins: 89% plastic in the pads, 18% in the plain plate.
  • Mounting: four #8 countersunk screws, 10 mm in from the corners. Three sit just outside the round flange (the screw heads clear its edge by 0.7 mm, so a driver goes straight on). The flange's point covers the lower-left one, so an Ø11 hole through the point lets that screw and the driver through; it shows on the face, below and left of the T. The lower-right screw is behind the docked wand: mount the holder with the wand off.
  • Not covered by the coupon: the housing and the start of the grip inside the deep opening. The housing room is cut from Tesla's CAD like the nose was; past the end of that CAD the grip is not modelled, and the opening there is as large at the rim as it was on the 150 mm version.
  • The flange stays whole: the docking room's top corner would have nicked 1.7 mm into its underside at the rim, so the cut stops at the flange. The docking and hold check is unchanged by that.

A smooth entry (2026-09-18)

You said the entry is rough and steps in. The step was mine: where Tesla's housing CAD ends, 48 mm from the nose tip, the cavity jumped 1.5 mm wider all round for the grip, which is not in the CAD. That jump sat just inside the mouth. It is gone: the sides and roof now widen steadily from the nose shoulder to the outer edge and arrive at the same size at the rim.

  • The floor is the one wall left alone. The hanging wand rests on it, and letting it fall away with the others changed how the wand hangs in the check (5.5° of droop instead of 3°). It keeps Tesla's line to the end of the housing CAD, exactly as printed, and the old ledge beyond that, right at the lip, is now a 4 mm ramp.
  • Against the cavity you called perfect, the new one only adds room, except for that ramp filling the ledge's corner (29 mm³, under the start of the grip). Docking and hold check: same way in with the wand grown 0.2 mm, same hanging pose (tip up 3°, 1.9 mm of the edge engaged), same 20 mm lift to come off. Docked clash: 0 mm³.

What is set

  • Plate 101.6 × 101.6 × 5 mm (4 in square), four countersunk holes for #8 screws, 10 mm in from the corners.
  • Drum Ø80, 75 mm out from the plate; teardrop flange Ø104 with its point to the lower left, blended into the drum with an R12 curve (R8 at the plate).
  • Tesla T recessed 1 mm into the flange face, 59 mm tall (57% of the round part, as on the sample), centred on the drum axis, from the official emblem artwork.
  • Wand 45° down and 15° off the wall; the mouth is 38 mm out from the wall, so the wand is hooked in last, outside the cable. The grip clears the wall by about 26 mm where it starts, 38 mm at its middle and 53 mm at its end.
  • Cleat depth: the cleat's holding wall is 31.75 mm (1.25 in) from the opening, measured along the cleat's wall. That seats the whole nose and the glossy housing behind it inside the drum; the cavity's deepest corner comes within 3 mm of the wall, into the 5 mm plate, and the top of the mouth runs about 8 mm up the blend under the flange, 3.6 mm short of the flange itself.
  • Cavity: the connector profile plus 0.5 mm on the sides, the floor and, over the tip, the roof; notch side down, button side up. From the tip outward the roof opens at 12° and the end wall leans back 12°: exactly the room a wand pivoting on its tip sweeps, and no more. Behind the nose shoulder the sides and roof open a further 10 mm per 100 mm out to the rim; the floor does not.
  • Cleat: a wedge cut to Tesla's lock pocket (spec: 9.71 ±0.2 wide and 6.2 ±0.2 long at its base, 4 ±0.2 deep; in Tesla's CAD it opens to 11.6 wide at the mouth and has a domed base). 10.6 mm wide at the floor narrowing to 9.3, 3.57 mm tall, ramp at 31° from the mouth side up to a sharp edge at the back, back face overhanging 15°. The nose stops 2.5 mm short of the cavity's end wall when hanging; that is the travel for pushing the pocket past the edge so the nose drops onto the cleat.
  • Cable: hangs in loops over the top of the drum, as on the sample; 47 mm of straight drum between the two blends, room for three Ø14.5 loops side by side, so the 18 ft cable (about six loops) stacks two deep.

How it docks, and why it now holds (2026-09-18)

You asked for the snug size at the end of the cavity to run further out. Checking that against Tesla's CAD turned up the reason the cleat has not been catching. The old roof was snug for 5 mm and then stepped up 5 mm so the nose could be lifted over the cleat. The hanging weight acts far out on the grip, so it levers the wand about the mouth's lower lip: tip up, pocket up. That is the same motion as lifting the nose over the cleat, run backwards. A path search over slide, lift and tilt (pipeline/insertion.py) gave: with the snug roof shorter than 3.9 mm the wand gets in, and its own weight takes it back out (the load has to rise only 0.2 mm); longer than that it holds, and cannot get in. At 5 mm the cavity was on the wrong side by 1.1 mm: it would have held, but the wand could not get in. No length of step roof does both.

So the snug part does have to reach further, as you said, and the wand has to dock by a motion the weight cannot undo: grip up, nose in, grip down. The roof is now the connector's size over the tip and opens only as far as that pivot sweeps. Compared with the old step it is closer to the wand for the first 25 mm (0.5 mm over the tip, 1.6 at 10 mm, 3.7 at 20 mm, where the step was 5.5 throughout) and wider beyond. With the wand grown 0.2 mm all round there is still a way in. Hanging, the weight turns the tip up 3° into the roof and stops: 1.9 mm of the 3.6 mm edge stays engaged, and the load would have to be raised 20 mm against gravity before the wand could come off.

The 50% longer cleat is retired: it is in the repository's history (commit f0ea071) and its files are removed. Tesla's pocket only takes the present cleat, and the catching problem was the roof, not the cleat's size.

Fit coupon

The coupon is the holder's nose cavity and the new cleat, cut off just past the nose shoulder, printed the way the holder prints (plate on the bed, tree supports in the cavity roof with Bambu Support For PLA/PETG on the second nozzle). Print time 1 h 36 min, 59 g in all: 55 g PETG and 4 g support material, from a real slice of coupon-print.3mf.

Result: it fits and holds. It proves the nose profile and its 0.5 mm clearance, the cleat in the lock pocket, docking grip-up over the cleat, and the hold: once docked, pulling the wand straight out or pressing the grip down should not free it; only raising the grip does. The deeper opening gets no coupon of its own (Brian, 2026-09-17) and is first tried on the full part.

Open

  • Lean: 15°, down from 20°. With the cleat 1.25 in deep the cavity is 65 mm tall inside the drum at 15° and 73 mm at 20°; at 20° its top would come out through the flange of the 75 mm drum.
  • Past the end of Tesla's housing CAD (48 mm from the tip) the grip is not modelled. The sides and roof have 1.6 mm extra room there and keep widening; the floor has 0.5 mm at that point and ramps to the same within 4 mm.
  • Printing: plate down on the bed. The cavity roof and the ring under the flange need support material (the X2D's support nozzle); everything else prints clean.
  • Next: print the 4 in version (holder-print.3mf), mount it, and try the wand with the cable on the drum.
